title.title: The spacetime Penrose inequality, in every dimension
title.subtitle: Claim: mass is at least that of a Schwarzschild black hole with the same minimum enclosing area, for all $n \ge 3$

beats.text: Initial data with a trapped boundary: its mass against its minimum enclosing area
Schwarzschild sits exactly on the curve; the claim is that nothing falls below it
The area is the least area of any enclosing cut, not the horizon's own area

achievement.label: Penrose's inequality (1973), enclosing-area form
achievement.context: Before: only the time-symmetric case, $n = 3$ (2001) and $3 \le n \le 7$ (Bray–Lee 2009)
achievement.note: Under dominant energy and decay hypotheses; 13 manuscripts, about 1,355 pages

verify.detail: Lean covers a supporting end-replacement construction and Schwarzschild examples, not the inequality
verify.ourCheck: We compared the Lean scope with the claim; we did not build it

sources.quote: for 3<=n<=7 by Bray-Lee (Duke Math. J. 148, 2009, arXiv:0705.1128)
only the Cha-Khuri-Sakovich end-replacement construction and Schwarzschild equality examples
must be stated with a minimal enclosing area rather than the horizon's own area

plain: A black hole must be heavy enough for its size: its mass can't fall below what its enclosing area demands

steps: Reshape the data so it looks like a moment frozen in time
There, mass and enclosing area can be controlled together
Compare every enclosing surface back to the original data

voice.text: Mass against smallest enclosing area: a Schwarzschild black hole sits exactly on this curve.
Reshape the data to look frozen in time, then compare every enclosing surface back.
Claimed: nothing falls below it, in every dimension.
